2C Event and tournament sanctioning - this chapter explains how a ranked event obtains SGF approval, and how it is then delivered

2C.1Shura Links, Red Sea, the Kingdom’s first island golf course

Sanctioning framework

How an event whose results count for rankings or qualification obtains SGF approval: one path of five SGF steps, from the eligibility check to the resultsWhy sanction: official recognition of results, a protected date on the national calendar, access to certified referees and scoring, promotion through SGF platforms, and compliance with venue license rules, avoiding fines and hosting bans

Five steps, select one
IP events only
Eligibility check1Hosting request2Hosting decision3Application4DecisionThe event5Results
ComplianceEnforced through the venue license, with fines for any breach

IP event: an event owned by an international rights holder, such as a professional tour

Delivery and officiating

How the organizer delivers a sanctioned event: three stages, prepare, deliver and report, each with actions for the teams that run the event

Three stages, select one
1PrepareBefore the event

Plans, approvals and people are in place, and systems are set up and tested

2DeliverTournament days

The event runs fairly and safely, for players, spectators and media

3ReportAfter the event

Results, reports and close-out are completed

2C.1.3 IP hosting approval - an internationally owned event needs its hosting contract approved before applying

!Mandatory
Eligibility check1Hosting request2Hosting decision3Application4DecisionThe event5ResultsCompliance
What this page settles

How an IP event gets its hosting contract approved

ATwo stepsA hosting request, then SGF’s decision
BFour requirementsWhat SGF assesses at step 2
ATwo steps
1
Step 1 · at least 15 months before the event

Hosting request

  • Submitted by the organizer to SGF
  • Includes the event details, the draft contract, the owner’s authorization and evidence for the four requirements
  • SGF can support the negotiation before the request
Open the hosting requestLink to follow
2
Step 2 · SGF decides within 90 days of receiving the hosting application

Hosting decision

  • SGF assesses the request against the four requirements below, after its quarterly Board meeting
  • The contract is signed only after approval
  • A rejection can be appealed directly to SGF
  • Once approved, the organizer applies for sanctioning at step 3 See 2C.1.4
SGF assesses all four at step 2 · all must be met
BFour requirements
I

Calendar compatibility

The event does not clash with other golf events already planned.

II

Transparent negotiation

The organizer follows SGF guidance when negotiating the contract, so that no other event is affected.

III

National image

The event, its leadership and its partners are consistent with the image of the Kingdom. Background checks apply.

IV

Alignment with SGF values

The event reflects the values of SGF, including respect and fair play, inclusivity, the development of Saudi talent, excellence and sustainability

Note: The 15-month timing is derived from the 12-month application deadline and the 90-day decision. Background checks run through the Ministry of SportSource: Saudi Golf Federation (Event Sanctioning Application Form, p1 and section 9, p11; SGF Event Sanctioning Overview, slides 16 and 17); Saudi Golf Federation (core values, SGF website)

AFeeAgreed with SGF before applying

AThe fee

The fee is agreed with SGF before the application is submitted. Professional events pay in line with their scale (to be validated with SGF); amateur events pay no fee

Amateur eventsNo fee
Professional eventsFee in line with event scale

Reduced fee

Events that strongly support SGF objectives, such as community engagement, sustainability or Saudi talent development, may receive a highly discounted or waived fee

Section 9 of the form confirms the agreed fee; SGF invoices it once the event is approved

BThe notice period

The application is submitted at least 12 months before the event, so that the event is placed in the national calendar

12months
before the event

Eligibility check1Hosting request2Hosting decision3Application4DecisionThe event5ResultsCompliance
What this page settles

How sanctioning is enforced, and what a breach costs

AEnforcementThrough the venue license, and which events it covers
BPenaltiesFines for the venue, up to a hosting ban
CChecksOrganizers and venues, before the event
AEnforcement
Riyadh Golf Club, set up for a tournament
In force · all year

The venue license on Riyadi

Every golf venue holds a license, which sets conditions for the events it hosts:

SGF approvalCompetition standardsStaffFlagsPlayer eligibilityResults submissionSGF logoBroadcast

Events that require approval

Under the test in 2C.1.2, an event requires SGF approval when its results count toward a ranking or qualify players for another tournament

Approval requiredEvents recorded on the Saudi Golf Ranking, and professional tour events
No approval requiredInformal events with no ranking or qualification, such as a corporate golf day
BPenalties

Charged to the venue, up to 120,000 and a hosting ban

Breach by the venueFirst breachRepeated breach
Hosting an event that needs sanctioning without SGF approval30,000and a hosting ban60,000and a hosting ban
Hosting an IP event without approval of its hosting contract60,000and a hosting ban120,000and a hosting ban
Failing to deliver an approved event to the agreed standardsUp to 10,000Up to 20,000

Fines apply per breach. Bans are decided case by case by the SGF Disciplinary Committee and can be appealed. Full penalty table in 2B.2

CChecks

Organizers and venues verify approvals before the event

Event organizers

Secure every approval in advance

Obtain sanctioning, and for an IP event approval of the hosting contract, before the event. Missing approvals result in fines for the venue.

✓
Venue operators

Verify approvals before agreeing to host

Request proof of SGF approval, and for an IP event of the approved hosting contract, before agreeing to host.

2C.2 Delivery and officiating - the organizer prepares, delivers and reports, and every operational area has a job at each stage

✓Guidance!Mandatory where flagged
2C.2
Sub-section 2C.2 starts here

Once sanctioned, the organizer delivers the event in three stages: prepare, deliver and report. Eight operational areas, covering every team involved in running a golf event, contribute at each stage. Items 2C.2.1 to 2C.2.7 are organized by stage.

Operational area
PrepareMonths before the event
2C.2.1Plans and approvals2C.2.2Event workforce2C.2.3Volunteers
DeliverTournament days
2C.2.4Officiating and play2C.2.5Spectators and media2C.2.6Safety and medical
ReportAfter the event
2C.2.7Post-event reporting
Competition management
!Set the course, local rules, entries and the draw; test scoring systems
!Rule on disputes and pace of play; record and post scores
!Submit the official results within 48 hours
On-course operations
Plan marshal positions and crossings; brief course teams and agree evacuation routes
Keep spectators quiet and on their paths; spot errant shots
No action
Player and caddie services
Plan player transport; register players and caddies, set up the practice range
Run transport, the locker room and the caddie lounge
No action
Spectator experience
Set up ticketing, gates, signage and information points
Check tickets, guide spectators, manage crowds and fan zones
No action
Safety, security and medical
!Prepare the safety plans and secure national approvals; set up medical posts and entry screening
!Run first aid posts, monitor the weather, handle incidents
!Submit the Ministry of Health event file
Commercial and hospitality
Confirm sponsor branding and activations; build merchandise and hospitality areas
Run merchandise sales and hospitality
No action
Media and broadcast
!Accredit the media and support broadcast set-up, under the SGF media and rights terms
Run the media center, broadcast data and photographer access
No action
Event services and workforce
Plan, recruit, train and equip the workforce; schedule shifts
Run workforce headquarters, supplies, parking and shuttles
!Recover equipment, debrief, rate volunteers and confirm their hours
Note: The eight operational areas are the teams that run an event. CPace and scoringFrom the first tee to verified scores
ARulings and decisions!Mandatory

Two kinds of decision, made by different people, with different routes to challenge them

Rules rulings

A referee applies the Rules of Golf to a player’s ball or stroke

Final and not subject to appeal. An incorrect ruling can be corrected only while the Rules of Golf allow, generally before the competition closes

Examples: relief from a cart path, or a penalty for a moved ball
Competition decisions

The Committee decides how the competition is run, with immediate effect

Appeals go to the appeal committee within 24 hours of the result; unresolved disputes may be referred to the Saudi Sports Arbitration Center within 21 days

Examples: player eligibility, suspension of play, results and disqualifications

Rules of Golf 20.2a and 20.2d · Referee licensing 2C.2.2

BMarshals✓Guidance

Marshals keep spectators on marked routes, quiet, and away from play

Walking marshals

Move with a group, keeping spectators quiet

Stationary marshals

Hold a hole, crossing or grandstand

Forecaddies

Spot where balls land, report every strike

CPace of play and scoring✓Guidance

Four steps keep groups on time and scores accurate

i
Tee off on timeThe starter sends each group off in draw order
ii
Keep pace in the roundPace is monitored against the set time par, and slow groups are reported to the Chief Referee
iii
Record scores liveWalking scorers report hole-by-hole scores, and scoreboards are updated live
iv
Verify and closeScorecards are checked and signed, and results are sent to SGF within 48 hours, see 2C.2.7

Roles: appointed 2C.2.2 · volunteers 2C.2.3

Note: Severe weather and evacuation are covered in 2C.2.6Source: Saudi Golf Federation (Referees Regulation; Competition Regulation, 31 August, disciplinary action and appeals; Competition and Championships Regulation, articles 5, 6 and 23); The R&A and USGA (Rules of Golf, Rules 20.2 and 5.6). 2C.2.5 Spectators and media - spectators watch quietly from behind the ropes, and media work within set access and recording rules

✓Guidance!Mandatory where flagged
1Prepare2C.2.1 to 2C.2.32Deliver2C.2.4 to 2C.2.63Report2C.2.7
What this page settles

Six conduct standards apply to spectators and to media, each backed by graduated sanctions

ASpectator etiquettePlay is observed from behind the ropes, in silence
BMedia etiquetteCoverage requires accreditation, without disturbing play
ASpectator etiquette!Four SGF rules flagged

Spectators watch quietly from behind the ropes, and never interfere with play

Position !Behind the ropes, about 25 m away; cross where marshals direct; off tees and greens
During a stroke !Still and silent until the group has played; applaud good play, never a mistake
PlayersNo advice to players; autographs only after the round, where designated
Ball and course !Never touch a ball or club; stay out of cordoned areas; use the bins
Phones and recordingSilent phones and calls away from play; no flash, video or live posts
Conduct and safety !Follow marshals; react at once to “Fore” and the siren; no heckling or abuse
EnforcementRising with the breach
1Course removalDisruptive behavior
2Grounds removalRepeat breach, no refund
3Future banOrganizer’s discretion
BMedia etiquette✓Guidance

Accredited media work inside the ropes without disturbing play

PositionInside the ropes only with that day’s credential, within arm’s length of the ropes
During a strokeSilent shutters; never on a tee or in a player’s line; move when asked
PlayersInterviews only after the scorecard is signed, with consent; never in the scoring area
EquipmentNo flash, tripods, ladders, drones or carts on the course
Recording and postingNo video of live play except the licensed broadcaster; no hole-by-hole posts
Conduct and accessCredential visible and not transferable; follow staff instructions
EnforcementRising with the breach
1Content takedownPosts or footage
2Credential revokedFor the person
3Outlet revokedFor the whole outlet
Note: SGF sets four spectator rules (flagged): outside the ropes, silent during shots, never touch a ball, and shelter at the siren; organizers enforce them. All other rules are recommended practice. Crowd management is part of the plans in 2C.2.1, marshals in 2C.2.4, and media rights in the application form, section 7 (2C.1.4)Source: Saudi Golf Federation (spectator etiquette); The R&A (The Open spectator code of conduct); USGA (Championships spectator conduct policy; media credential regulations); European Golf Association (spectator policy); PGA TOUR (fan codes of conduct; World Wide Technology Championship spectator etiquette; Media Regulations, 2026); The R&A and USGA (Rules of Golf)

CSevere weather✓Guidance

Play stops at the siren, and spectators are moved to safe areas

Conditions that can stop play

Lightning and thunderstormsSandstorms and dustExtreme heatHeavy rain and floodingHigh winds

Siren signals

One prolonged noteStop play immediately
Two short notesResume play
Three consecutive notesNormal suspension

With lightning within about 10 km, everyone moves to shelter. Play resumes 30 minutes after the last strike

Siren signals follow the Rules of Golf model local rule J-1. Guidance, not an SGF requirement

Builds on the minimum
